numericalDegree.note: Twenty-one reduces to three (2+1), linking it to the Empress's creation and the Lovers' union. It is the degree at which the cycle is complete.

courtFunction.note: The World is not a court card; it is the archetype of completion.

figureType.value: A dancing human figure within a wreath, with four creatures at the corners
figureType.note: The human is the figure of the completed self; the four creatures are the elements that hold the completion in place.

posture.value: Dancing, one leg crossed, arms holding wands
posture.note: The posture is one of dynamic balance. The World is not a static completion; it is a completion in motion.

gesture.value: Holding two wands, one in each hand
gesture.note: The gesture is one of balance: the two wands are held, one in each hand, the will and the matter finally equal.

gaze.value: Facing forward or slightly inward
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the completed self. The figure is looking at the whole, not at the parts.

movementDirection.note: The movement is circular, the movement of the completed cycle. The World is the card of the return.

centralObject.value: The wreath
centralObject.note: The wreath is the central object, the whole cycle embraced. It is the structure of completion.

heldObject.note: The wands are held, one in each hand. The holding is the holding of the two poles, brought into balance.

creature.value: Four creatures: a lion, a bull, an eagle, and a man (or angel)
creature.note: The four creatures are the four elements, the fixed points of the completed world. They are the guardians of the whole.

tool.note: The tools are the wands of will and matter. They are the instruments of the completed balance.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The World's law is not written; it is enacted in the dance.

landscape.value: A wreath and a sky with four creatures
landscape.note: The landscape is the cosmic whole: the wreath, the sky, the four corners. The World is the card of the complete world.

architecture.note: There is no architecture. The World is in the open cosmos, not in a city or a temple.

threshold.note: The wreath is the threshold between the cycle that has been completed and the next that is to begin. The figure stands within it.

celestialBody.value: The four creatures (the four fixed signs of the zodiac)
celestialBody.note: The four creatures are the celestial markers of the four corners. They are the structure of the cosmos.

weather.note: The weather is fair. The World is the card of the clear completion.

symmetry.value: Balanced and symmetrical (the four creatures at the corners)
symmetry.note: The composition is symmetrical: the four creatures at the corners, the figure in the centre. The symmetry is the symmetry of the whole.

repetitionCount.note: The number four is the number of the fixed elements. The four creatures are the corners of the completed world.

verticalAxis.value: The wreath above and below the figure
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis is the axis of the whole: the wreath surrounds the figure, above and below.

horizontalAxis.value: The four creatures at the four corners
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the plane of the four elements: the creatures hold the four corners of the world.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The World is upright and whole.

clothing.value: A light scarf or veil (the figure is nude or lightly draped)
clothing.note: The figure is nude or lightly draped. The clothing is the mark of the completed self, at ease in its own body.

nudity.value: Present (the figure is nude or lightly draped)
nudity.note: The nudity is the nudity of the completed self, the absence of shame and the presence of wholeness.

crown.note: There is no crown. The World's authority is not social; it is the authority of completion.

wound.note: There is no wound. The World is the card of healing and wholeness.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figure is free within the wreath.

water.note: There is no water. The World's element is earth and spirit, not water.

fire.note: There is no fire. The World's heat is the heat of completion, not of passion.

vegetation.note: The vegetation is the wreath, the living circle of the completed cycle.

stone.note: There is no stone. The World is the card of the living whole, not of the built structure.

polarity.note: The World's remedy-pair is the Fool: she is completion, he is beginning. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the World's completion is the Fool's beginning: the completion is not the end; it is the threshold of the next step.

prescribedAct.value: Mark one thing as complete today, and let yourself feel the wholeness before you begin the next.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of completion. The World's lesson is that the cycle must be acknowledged before it can begin again.

detailedReading: The World is the card of completion and wholeness, and its detailed features show how that completion is structured. Its elemental register is earth and spirit: the wreath, the four creatures, and the dancing figure mark it as the card of completion. The numerical degree is twenty-one — the degree at which the cycle is complete — and the posture is dancing, one leg crossed, arms holding wands. The gesture is one of balance: the two wands held, one in each hand. The central object is the wreath, the whole cycle embraced. The creatures are the four elements, the guardians of the whole. The landscape is the cosmic whole: the wreath, the sky, the four corners. There is no written word, no wound, and no binding: the World's law is enacted, not written; it is not suffering; and the figure is free within the wreath. The symmetry of the composition is the symmetry of the whole. The prescribed act follows from this: mark one thing as complete today, and let yourself feel the wholeness before you begin the next. The remedy is beginning — the Fool's new step — because the completion needs to be corrected by the recognition that it is also a threshold.
